data.abstract: In 1990, Congress enacted statutory amendments to adjust the maximum civil penalty amounts authorized under the Consumer Product Safety Act (CPSA), the Federal Hazardous Substances Act (FHSA), and the Flammable Fabrics Act (FFA). On August 14, 2008, the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 2008 (CPSIA) increased the maximum civil penalty amounts to $100,000 for each violation and $15,000,000 for any related series of violations. The CPSIA tied the effective date of the new amounts to the earlier of the date on which final regulations are issued, or 1 year after August 14, 2008. The new amounts became effective on August 14, 2009. The CPSIA also revised the starting date, from December 1, 1994 to December 1, 2011, and December 1 of each fifth calendar year thereafter, on which the Commission must prescribe and publish in the Federal Register, the schedule of maximum authorized penalties. On December 1, 2021, the CPSC published increased maximum authorized civil penalty amounts of $120,000 for each violation and $17,150,000 for any related series of violations. As calculated in accordance with the amendments, the new amounts are $140,000 for each violation and $20,350,000 for any related series of violations.

observations.title: Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines

data.abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model GE90-110B1 and GE90- 115B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an aborted takeoff due to left engine failure caused by liberation of the interstage high-pressure turbine (HPT) rotor seal rim. This proposed AD would require determining the recalculated service life of the interstage HPT rotor seal and, depending on the results, replacing the interstage HPT rotor seal with a part eligible for installation. For certain engine populations, as an alternative to replacing the interstage HPT rotor seal, this proposed AD would require initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections of the interstage HPT rotor seal for cracks and, depending on the results, removing the interstage HPT rotor seal from service. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

observations.title: Technical Updates to the RCRA Hazardous Waste Permitting Regulations-Permitting Technical Updates Rule

data.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing technical updates to the regulations implementing the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) governing hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs), as well as associated permitting requirements. The proposal also includes a few conforming technical updates to the generator and transporter regulations. The RCRA hazardous waste TSDF permitting regulations have remained largely unchanged for over three decades, despite evolving standards and practices. Collectively, these revisions are intended to address inadvertent errors, remove obsolete references, reflect current information and standards, and implement targeted updates to the RCRA permitting regulations to improve clarity, consistency, and efficiency in the hazardous waste TSDF permitting program. Through a separate Federal Register document, EPA will be seeking input on areas in the RCRA permitting program and permitting regulations to consider for permitting policy or regulatory reform. This proposed rule helps clear the way for potential future regulatory actions that could improve implementation of the RCRA hazardous waste permitting program. It serves as a maintenance action and does not preclude the possibility of future permitting reform.
